title: A bounded-time decider for decoding
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite Turing machine $D$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $a$ such that for each Boolean string $\alpha$, some Boolean value $b$ is output as the single-symbol word $[b]$ within $a(|\alpha|+1)^a$ steps. If $b$ is false, decoding $\alpha$ returns the fallback code; if $b$ is true, the scan of $\alpha$ succeeds and returns a suffix.
